scope: 19 distinct scored nominations and 2 hard-exclusion nominations. Main book records only; related-title widgets and incidental review references are research context.

notes: Extensive references and explicit physical quantities support the industrial account; selective transition comparisons prevent a higher mark.
Energy, food, materials and global production are connected through physical inputs, conversion losses and supply chains.
Useful for checking scale, substitution limits and hidden dependencies; treatment of alternative pathways is incomplete.
Explains embodied inputs and industrial constraints; risk comparisons and transition dynamics receive less complete causal treatment.
Seven focused chapters compress a large research programme; substantial supporting notes earn their space.
The physical dependencies and scale calculations remain useful beyond current forecasts; date-specific numbers require updating.
Direct match to energy, industrial production, materials, logistics and quantitative reasoning.
Long-established specialist synthesis is supported by substantive engagement in an energy journal, including criticism.
A clear sequence moves from inputs to production, interdependence and uncertainty.
Definitions and units are generally controlled; dismissive language and the claim to an agenda-free perspective reduce precision.
books.case: The useful payload is a quantitative map of the material economy: test a proposed substitution against physical throughput, energy conversion and infrastructure requirements. The Energy Journal review supports the accessible synthesis while identifying missing treatment of alternative production routes. Its reviewer works in energy research at Saudi Aramco; this is relevant context, not independent proof of the transition forecast.
books.objection: Daramus challenges primary-energy comparisons, the neglect of innovation rates and the use of average deaths to compare terrorism with traffic accidents. These objections matter to this reader. They reduce evidence, mechanism and precision scores. They do not establish that the core account of present industrial dependencies is false, and the score does not endorse every forecast.
books.eligibility: A sustained explanation for general readers, not an energy-engineering manual or training text. No serious failure of the central material-dependency account is established. V1/V2 concerns about extrapolation remain limitations rather than demonstrated grounds to discard the whole book; V3/V4/V5 do not apply to its principal explanatory purpose.
books.theme: T11=0: environmental consequences are one part of a wider industrial account, not its predominant subject. T12=0: energy and material production are central; politics and finance are auxiliary. H13=0: a contemporary, cross-period argument, not one historical episode.

notes: Uses historical sources, research and practitioner interviews; specialist reception supports the synthesis, without proving every large causal claim.
Connects materials, mechanization, labour, mathematics, chemical innovation, commercial institutions and trade.
Shows how bottlenecks, complements and demand move invention across industries; less direct guidance on choosing among future technologies.
Production steps and labour requirements explain why particular innovations matter; some civilizational effects remain interpretive.
Seven process-led chapters keep the broad history compact and cumulative.
A long historical account of production and exchange has little dependence on a current prediction.
Strong match to manufacturing, scaling, precision of process, trade and industrial innovation.
A well-researched journalistic synthesis with specialist review support, rather than the author's own technical research programme.
The progression from fibre to production and exchange gives the breadth a clear structure.
Concrete processes and distinctions carry the explanation without a large invented vocabulary.
books.case: Textiles provide a connected account of industrial civilization: biological inputs become fibres, labour turns them into thread and cloth, chemistry changes their properties, and trade creates incentives and institutions. The Antiquity assessment confirms both the global scope and the shift from manufacturing to exchange. This is especially useful for seeing how an apparently ordinary product can organize a whole technical and commercial system.
books.objection: A history seen through one material family can overstate that family's causal importance. The inspected reviews support the research and architecture but do not establish a controlled test of the claim that textiles made civilization. E=18 and M=11 retain this limitation; no perfect evidence or mechanism score is awarded.
books.eligibility: A general historical explanation. Descriptions of spinning, weaving and dyeing explain the narrative; the book is not structured as training in those procedures. No serious V1–V5 trigger was established. Authorial political associations alone are not evidence of ideological capture.
books.theme: T11=0: slavery, gender and environmental effects are subsidiary to global textile production. T12=0: manufacturing and innovation are central; commerce and political controls explain applications. H13=0: the account crosses prehistory, industrialization and modern production without one central period.

reviews: Publishers Weekly review of the US title
notes: First-hand manufacturing expertise and concrete process accounts support reliability; a new popular synthesis has limited independent checking.
Connects product design, factories, production trade-offs, shipping and delivery.
Volume-versus-variety and localization trade-offs transfer well to other production systems.
Explains processes and supply-chain constraints; the general-reader format limits engineering depth.
Everyday-product narratives are productive, but some elementary explanation has low marginal value for this reader.
Production trade-offs endure; current examples and forecasts have had limited time to be tested.
Manufacturing, logistics and scaling directly match the requested centre.
Cambridge manufacturing scholarship and industrial engagement directly match the subject.
A conversational journey through familiar products gives complex supply chains a readable form.
Concrete examples clarify trade-offs without requiring specialist jargon.
books.case: A strong recent candidate for understanding the complete production system behind everyday goods. The inspected reviews identify process explanations and explicit choices between scale, variety and location. Your Life Is Manufactured and the US How Things Are Made are one work, not two recommendations.
books.objection: Introductory explanation and limited long-term scrutiny constrain the positive score. The verified UK aggregate remains below 1,000, so the obscurity rule removes five points. The smaller US aggregate is not added to it.
books.eligibility: A narrative explanation of manufacturing for outsiders, not a course or operating guide. Sustainability discussion is present but the principal structure is explanatory. No serious veto is established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: industrial production and delivery are central. H13=0: contemporary explanatory account. The 2026 paperback does not reset the 2025 original year.

notes: A researched popular history, but precision as the master explanation is broader than the evidence demonstrated in the inspected material.
Links measurement, machine tools, interchangeability and modern scientific instruments.
The dependence of scale and reliability on tolerances is highly reusable.
Concrete engineering cases explain enabling constraints; the tolerance ladder is not a complete causal theory.
Memorable cases earn most of the length, though personality and historical detail dilute the mechanisms.
Measurement and interchangeability remain durable industrial problems.
Precision, reliability and manufacturing are direct matches.
An experienced historical synthesist, not a specialist authority in every engineering field covered.
The progression through increasingly fine tolerances is memorable and readable.
The dramatic precision framing and unresolved technical-error reports warrant restraint.
books.case: Explains why better measurement and machine tools enable later technologies. The title is also published as Exactly. This is a promising fit but does not receive a near-perfect score merely because precision appears explicitly in the user's interests.
books.objection: Kirkus characterizes it as a popular tour rather than scholarship. Reader reports of technical errors were located but not all could be checked against the relevant edition; they are unresolved leads, not asserted corrections or a proven V1 failure. The narrative also risks making one enabling factor explain too much.
books.eligibility: Historical narrative, not precision-engineering training. No serious central epistemic failure is verified; transferable mechanisms are clear. No other veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: global industrial precision is central. H13=0: cross-period account from early machine tools to modern instruments, not one bounded historical period.

notes: Well-supported historical cases; retrospective chains are not controlled evidence that the same patterns predict new inventions.
Shows links between materials, technical capabilities, production and social consequences across six domains.
Useful for identifying enabling technologies and unexpected spillovers, less useful for forecasting their direction.
Explains dependency chains well but sometimes simplifies the underlying physical mechanism.
Six bounded themes and an illustrated format keep the account compact.
Historical interdependence and technological complements do not depend on current fashion.
Innovation, materials and technological infrastructure fit directly.
An established synthesist with strong narrative reach, not a primary researcher in each domain.
The connected stories make complex technological ancestry memorable.
Readable prose occasionally substitutes wonder for a precise physical explanation.
books.case: The 2014 adult book follows glass, refrigeration, sound, cleanliness, time and light to show how inventions create options in other fields. It is a stronger fit than a lone-genius narrative, but a physicist will find some mechanisms elementary.
books.objection: Kirkus explicitly notes occasional oversimplified scientific language. Attractive chains of historical influence can also reflect selection after the outcome is known. Those limits reduce M and P and keep the book below 90. The separate 2018 young-reader adaptation is not used for either year or Amazon identity.
books.eligibility: An explanatory history for general readers, not technical instruction. Transferable dependencies are substantial; no serious V1–V5 trigger established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: neither the cleanliness chapter nor the sound/media examples dominate the six-part technological account. H13=0: broad cross-period scope.

notes: Empirical regularities deserve attention; universality and causal extrapolation into social systems remain disputed.
Connects networks, biological constraints, cities and companies, with weaker integration of institutions and changing incentives.
Useful dimensional and scaling heuristics, but limited support for direct business or policy prediction.
Scaling correlations are not always accompanied by a persuasive causal derivation.
Lengthy digressions and repeated claims reduce density for a mathematically trained reader.
Scaling questions endure; some proposed universal social laws may not.
Scaling is central, but much space goes to familiar popular physics, biology and cities.
The author is a leading contributor to the research being explained; authority does not settle its generality.
Accessible diagrams and stories coexist with a long, digressive structure.
Clear qualitative language sometimes implies more universality than the evidence supports.
books.case: A direct thematic match with a weaker score after checking the inference. Dyson distinguishes successful description of patterns from incomplete explanation; Fix challenges the move from observed company and city data to broad laws.
books.objection: The user's physics background makes the absence of derivations and the repeated popular exposition especially costly. The claims are not dismissed solely because they are ambitious, but they do not earn near-perfect evidence or mechanism points.
books.eligibility: A popular explanatory account, not a specialist monograph or course. The inspected criticism limits particular extrapolations without establishing that the whole cross-domain inquiry must be vetoed. No V2–V5 trigger established.
books.theme: T11=0: urban and environmental applications share space with organisms and firms rather than predominating. T12=0: scaling and networks are central. H13=0: no single historical period.

reviews: Dan Gordon: Issues in Science and Technology
notes: A carefully developed argument with engineering examples; incomplete engagement with prior scholarship limits its novelty claims.
Combines physical phenomena, components, engineering domains and economic change.
Recombination and complementary capabilities offer portable ways to understand innovation.
Explains recursive problem-solving and dependencies; broad evolution claims are harder to test.
A compact argument with some repetition around recursion and definitions.
Technological recombination remains useful independent of current products.
Technology and invention are the central objects of explanation.
Direct expertise in economics of technology and complexity, with substantive critical review.
Cumulative but abstract and less fluent than the strongest narrative histories.
Terms and distinctions are deliberately defined, even when the vocabulary is demanding.
books.case: A sustained theory of technology as combinations of existing components that exploit physical effects. The publisher provides the opening argument; Gordon's review finds the engineering chapters productive while questioning the completeness of the scholarship.
books.objection: This is not a demonstrated universal law of innovation. Gordon identifies omitted predecessors and limited value in some recursive terminology; Kirkus notes the demanding presentation. The Amazon count also triggers −5.
books.eligibility: The publisher's excerpt is an explanatory argument, not a procedure or engineering course. Academic language alone does not trigger hard exclusion 2. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: the centre is technological invention and economic evolution, not general philosophy; conceptual framing is the method. H13=0: timeless, cross-period argument.

notes: Expert materials knowledge and historical research support the cases; broad cultural consequences are harder to establish causally.
Connects material properties, inventions and changes in daily life across eight technologies.
Useful for recognizing unintended effects, with fewer explicit strategic tools.
Strong explanations of material properties; social feedback is often illustrated rather than tested.
Rich examples and illustrations, with some biography and introductory material beyond this reader's needs.
Historical mechanisms and material constraints are durable.
Materials, communications, precision and computing are direct matches.
Materials-science expertise directly supports the technical content.
Eight invention-centred stories provide an accessible structure.
Clear explanations keep the scientific concepts concrete.
books.case: Pairs changes in materials with changes in human behaviour, using clocks, rails, communication, recording and computing among its cases. The selected paperback is 2021, but the work originated in 2020.
books.objection: The human stories sometimes take priority over detailed industrial mechanism. This is a useful explanatory collection, not a tightly tested theory of technological change. The Amazon count adds a five-point deduction.
books.eligibility: General narrative science history, not materials training. Inclusion of overlooked inventors and racial effects does not itself establish political activism or ideological capture. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: racial and social consequences are among several effects, not the predominant subject. T12=0: material inventions are central. H13=0: cross-period technological cases.

notes: Well-documented failures support caution; selecting failures does not establish the strongest stagnation claim.
Connects technical feasibility, deployment, unintended harm and adoption.
Highly reusable distinctions between invention, successful scaling and durable benefit.
Explains failure modes well; forecasting the aggregate pace of innovation is less secure.
A brief, organized case-based argument earns most of its length.
Failure mechanisms endure; judgments about contemporary AI and energy technologies can date quickly.
Invention and industrial adoption directly fit.
Deep expertise across energy and technological history supports the synthesis.
The categories of failed expectation give the cases a clear structure.
Usually precise, but pessimistic generalization can outrun the case evidence.
books.case: A concise account of why invention is not the same as useful innovation. The IET review supports its historical engineering interest; Gates agrees on deployment constraints but disputes the treatment of AI, technological convergence and newer energy options.
books.objection: Gates is an interested investor, not a neutral arbiter, and his own forecasts are not proof. His objections still identify a genuine inferential gap: historical failures alone cannot establish that new combinations will disappoint. This constrains E and R.
books.eligibility: Historical and explanatory nonfiction, not an innovation playbook. The failure cases have a durable payload; no serious central V1–V5 trigger established.
books.theme: T11=0: harmful environmental effects form one class of examples, not the whole book. T12=0: technological invention and adoption are central. H13=0: multiple periods rather than one historical episode.

notes: Physical geography is well grounded; some large historical links remain selective and vulnerable to determinism.
Connects geology, resources, agriculture, movement and trade.
Useful environmental constraints on strategy, with limited direct decision tools.
Strong physical enabling conditions; institutions and human choices receive less complete causal treatment.
A broad, readable survey with some basic science and loosely linked cases.
Geological and resource constraints are durable.
Geography and resources fit, but less attention goes to engineering and production than in the leading candidates.
Scientific expertise supports the physical account; historical synthesis spans beyond the author's primary field.
Readable stories make long timescales approachable.
Clear prose, though broad causal language requires care.
books.case: Examines how the physical Earth constrains human history. The US and UK subtitles differ; the verified UK paperback is the same Lewis Dartnell work.
books.objection: A physical constraint is not a sufficient cause of a political or social outcome. The Chemistry World indexed assessment also questions the unity of the overall narrative. The full review page was not accessible, so no unseen criticism is claimed.
books.eligibility: A general explanatory history, not geology training. No serious veto is established by the inspected evidence; causal overreach remains a scoring limitation.
books.theme: T11=0: physical geography and geological constraints are central, not ecology or environmental activism. T12=0: political examples are applications. H13=0: deep-time and modern examples have no single central period.

books.format: hardcover; no verified available English paperback found
notes: Extensive interviews support reporting; access and success-selection can bias the explanation.
Links chip design, software platforms, organizational practice and markets, with less depth on external supply constraints.
Reusable lessons about platform commitment, feedback and long investment horizons.
Useful operating mechanisms, but the account cannot isolate leadership effects from favourable market conditions.
A compact company history focuses on decisions and execution.
Historical lessons endure; the current AI boom makes the ending less settled.
Computing, high technology and industrial organization directly fit.
Experienced technology reporting and access support authority; long specialist scrutiny is limited.
A clear company narrative makes technical and managerial choices readable.
Concrete reporting is stronger than claims of a universal management formula.
books.case: An account of Nvidia's development and organizational methods based on interviews with people involved. It is distinct from Stephen Witt's later book and earns no extra credit merely for covering a highly valued company.
books.objection: Independent adverse review access was limited. Publisher and author claims of extensive access establish scope, not correctness. The positive score therefore retains a meaningful evidence discount, and book-level confidence is low.
books.eligibility: High-tech company history rather than a procedural management manual. The science/high-tech biography exception is relevant, though the organizational payload also passes V3 directly. Historical engineering decisions provide value beyond current AI publicity, so V4 is not established.
books.theme: T11=0: US company setting has global technological influence. T12=0: computing and company execution are central, not finance or a media celebrity. H13 uses 2024 as the assessed endpoint of the company history; endpoint confidence moderate.

books.format: hardcover; identified paperback is scheduled for 2027
reviews: Kevin Gardiner: Society of Professional Economists
notes: Extensive historical sourcing; broad causal claims are difficult to identify and test across disparate societies.
Connects invention, scaling, organizations, competition and state capacity.
The distinction between exploring new technologies and coordinating deployment transfers well.
A plausible institutional mechanism, with some causal compression of complex historical outcomes.
Substantial notes support the synthesis; the long survey includes repeated illustrations.
The institutional tension is durable, while current AI and national outlooks remain unsettled.
Innovation, production and scaling are central.
Economic-history expertise directly supports the project, though this book is still recent.
Readable country cases sustain a very broad argument.
Occasional claims of having established a general historical law are too strong.
books.case: Studies the tension between decentralized experimentation and the coordination required to scale production. The publisher record dates the original work to 2025; a later paperback cannot reset that age.
books.objection: Gardiner praises the synthesis but challenges its causal confidence and compressed explanation of the Soviet collapse. The book remains a hypothesis supported by historical cases, not a reliably identified law. The low Amazon count costs five points.
books.eligibility: A general historical argument, not a textbook. It credits both coordination and experimentation; the inspected evidence does not establish an allegiance-dependent or activist central argument. No veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: explicitly comparative, not single-nation history. T12=0: institutions are mechanisms explaining technological development, which is central. H13=0: broad cross-period synthesis over many societies.

notes: Developer interviews and contribution patterns support the account; selection and broader generalization remain limitations.
Connects software production, maintenance, incentives, attention and organizational forms.
Maintenance constraints and contributor-versus-user growth are highly transferable to digital infrastructure.
Explains why usage can grow faster than maintenance capacity and how this changes incentives.
A focused argument with productive classifications and limited digression.
Maintenance and scarce attention are durable constraints despite changing platforms.
Direct fit to computation, digital infrastructure and production scaling.
Research and practical GitHub experience support authority; less mature scholarly testing than the strongest classics.
Clear categories organize a complex collection of project types.
Definitions distinguish open access from unlimited contributor attention.
books.case: Examines who bears the maintenance burden of open software. The publisher describes a research-based analysis rather than a coding guide; Lehman's review shows how its project classifications connect audience growth to scarce maintainer time.
books.objection: Not every open project follows the same pattern, and extending the argument to all internet creators is less secure than the software evidence. The selected Amazon count remains below 1,000.
books.eligibility: An explanatory account of software production and its economics, not programming instruction or a specialist operating manual. No serious V1–V5 trigger established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: software production and maintenance are central; online media and governance are applications. H13=0: a contemporary explanatory argument, not a bounded historical chronicle.

reviews: Chris Wellisz: IMF Finance and Development
notes: Ground-level reporting is valuable, but one-sided causal allocation and omitted competing explanations materially weaken inference.
Connects factories, ports, trucking, rail, inventory and labour arrangements.
Illustrates vulnerability and inventory trade-offs, with less reliable guidance on remedies.
Some concrete bottlenecks are explained; profit-seeking is too often treated as a sufficient explanation.
Detailed logistics reporting is diluted by repeated denunciation and local background.
Supply-chain resilience is durable; the pandemic-specific frame and remedies are less so.
Production logistics and constraints fit directly despite the political framing.
Experienced economics reporting and field access support the descriptive material.
Following a shipment gives the complex system a strong narrative line.
Moralized language obscures distinctions among incentives, market power and physical bottlenecks.
books.case: The shipment narrative exposes real interdependence across factories, ports and inland transport. Positive reporting value is retained in this counterfactual score; the veto does not erase it.
books.objection: Wellisz identifies repeated denunciations and the concluding programme of stronger unions and antitrust enforcement. Grabow, writing from an opposing policy perspective, alleges missing regulatory and demand-side explanations. His ideological label is not accepted as proof; the repeated advocacy independently described by Wellisz supports the narrower V5 decision.
books.eligibility: Passes both hard exclusions: narrative nonfiction, not a logistics manual. Veto V5, moderate confidence: the central account advances a sustained political-economic reform case through the supply-chain narrative. No additional V1 or V2 veto is asserted without stronger checking of the book's complete treatment of counterevidence.
books.theme: T11=0: the US-centred narrative has global supply-chain implications, and disease is a trigger rather than the principal subject. T12=−10: corporate power and labour-political reform organize the central diagnosis. H13 uses 2022 as the assessed endpoint of the pandemic episode, moderate confidence; P14 uses 2024.

notes: A quantitative historical synthesis grounded in extensive research; very large comparative claims retain uncertainty.
Explicitly links population, agriculture, energy, economies and their interactions.
Useful for distinguishing sequences, complements and constraints in large transformations.
Mechanisms and enabling factors matter throughout, though not every broad association is identified causally.
Dense evidence earns much of the length; some descriptive accumulation reduces efficiency.
Long-run structural transformations remain useful beyond current news.
Energy, food production and technological-economic change are strong matches.
Direct specialist standing and a substantial related research programme.
A coherent analytical framework, but denser and less immediately readable than the popular synthesis.
Quantities and long-run distinctions are generally controlled.
books.case: A five-transition framework for explaining the modern world. The author's introduction and contents establish the integrated scope, rather than a specialist instructional purpose.
books.objection: The breadth demands compression, and quantitative association does not settle the direction of causation. The density and readability scores are lower than for How the World Really Works. Obscurity adds a further five-point deduction.
books.eligibility: A sustained interdisciplinary account, not a course, reference manual or narrow technical monograph. Environmental consequences are analyzed within that account; no central activism veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: environment is one of five interacting transitions rather than the predominant topic. T12=0: material and technological transformation is central. H13=0: broad cross-period global account.

notes: Economic-complexity research supports the production-network argument; the physics-to-economics synthesis is broader than its direct tests.
Connects physical order, knowledge, organizations, networks and productive capabilities.
Useful for thinking about distributed know-how and the capabilities needed to make complex products.
Constraints on individual knowledge and coordination are mechanisms; information as a universal explanation is less secure.
Compact and ambitious, but some conceptual detours delay the practical argument.
Distributed productive knowledge remains a durable economic constraint.
Physics, computation and industrial capability are direct matches.
The author contributes directly to economic-complexity research.
The progression from physical order to economies is demanding and occasionally discontinuous.
Definitions matter, but familiar physical terms can suggest stronger equivalence across domains than is demonstrated.
books.case: Recasts productive capability as distributed knowledge and know-how embodied in networks and products. The original year is 2015; the linked paperback is later.
books.objection: A physicist should distinguish a useful information analogy from a causal derivation of prosperity. The reviewed synthesis does not justify awarding full mechanistic or evidential attainment. The Amazon count remains below 1,000.
books.eligibility: A general argumentative account, not a mathematical economics textbook or specialist methods manual. No serious central veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: productive capability is central, not financial markets or philosophy as the end subject. H13=0: general theory with examples from multiple periods.

notes: Extensive access supports the reported chronology; access bias and retrospective success selection remain material.
Connects parallel computation, software, organizational commitment and markets, with less depth on the complete supply chain.
Long investment horizons and software-hardware complements transfer well.
Explains consequential technical and organizational choices without isolating their effects experimentally.
A compact biography centres on major decisions and technological change.
Earlier engineering history has lasting value; the AI-era ending remains unsettled.
Direct fit to computing, technological leverage and industrial organization.
Experienced investigative reporting and access, with limited time for specialist scrutiny of this book.
A focused protagonist and sequence of technical bets produce a strong narrative.
Concrete reporting keeps much of the technical story accessible and disciplined.
books.case: A separate Nvidia history from Tae Kim's, focused on Huang and the transition from graphics hardware to AI infrastructure. The primary interview helps distinguish the author's reporting from publisher promotion.
books.objection: A successful company's current dominance does not validate every leadership practice or prove a general formula. The 2024 endpoint sits inside an unresolved industry expansion, so durability is below maximum. This is Stephen Witt's nonfiction work, not Jacques Futrelle's similarly titled fiction.
books.eligibility: High-tech biography and business history, not procedural instruction. It has transferable technical and organizational payload; earlier history prevents a V4 veto based solely on current AI attention. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=0: US company setting with global technological influence. T12=0: computing and industrial development are central. H13 uses 2024 as the assessed endpoint: the publisher frames the story around Nvidia's ascent to the highest market value in June 2024. Endpoint confidence moderate; original publication is separately 2025.

reviews: Kirkus review of the US edition
notes: Expert explanation of well-established material properties; simplified presentation prevents full attainment.
Strong materials-to-application links, but less integration of trade, institutions and production systems.
Useful design constraints and material intuition, with fewer strategic models.
Explains how structure and properties enable applications at an accessible level.
A compact selection of materials with little unnecessary technical apparatus.
The basic material mechanisms are durable.
Materials and engineering fit, but elementary physics adds less for this reader.
Materials-science expertise directly supports the book's core.
Everyday objects anchor clear and memorable explanations.
Controlled explanations connect concrete experience to physical properties.
books.case: A compact explanation of familiar materials by a specialist. The original UK publication is 2013; the 2014 US release is not the age used for scoring.
books.objection: High technical reliability does not compensate for lower systems breadth and limited novelty for a theoretical physicist. It is not scored as a near-perfect strategic synthesis merely because it is an excellent popular science book.
books.eligibility: General explanatory nonfiction with narrative examples, not a materials-science course or technical reference. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: material properties and useful applications are central. H13=0: explanatory, cross-period account.

reviews: Kirkus review of the US title
Authorized preview: original UK publication in 2018
notes: Expert explanation of established liquid properties, simplified for a broad audience.
Connects properties to everyday and engineering applications, with limited institutional or industrial-system breadth.
Useful physical intuition, but fewer general strategic mechanisms.
Strong explanations of fluid behaviour and material interactions at a popular level.
The bounded journey frame keeps the selection compact and purposeful.
Fundamental liquid properties have lasting value.
Engineering applications fit; much underlying physics will be familiar.
Direct materials-science expertise supports the explanations.
The airplane journey provides a clear narrative device.
Concrete, accessible language keeps properties and effects connected.
books.case: The UK Liquid and US Liquid Rules are the same work. It explains liquids through an airplane journey and associated materials. The original UK year is 2018, preceding the 2019 US edition.
books.objection: The main limitation is fit, not quality: this is accessible physical science with less industrial or strategic integration. Its verified Amazon aggregate also triggers the five-point obscurity deduction.
books.eligibility: Narrative popular science, not a fluid-mechanics textbook or operating manual. No serious veto established.
books.theme: T11=T12=0: liquids and their applications are central. H13=0: no bounded historical period.

excluded.title: The Knowledge
excluded.author: Lewis Dartnell
excluded.reason: The published book excerpt explicitly teaches procedures for reconstructing a technology, within a work organized as a restart guide. The conceptual explanation is substantial, so the boundary is closer than for a conventional manual; its central purpose remains rebuilding capabilities through instruction. The author's photography chapter and the independent account of practical food-preservation and microscope instructions support hard exclusion 2. The hypothetical catastrophe does not make this a fiction exclusion.

excluded.title: The Science of Scaling
excluded.author: Benjamin Hardy; Blake Erickson
excluded.reason: The publisher explicitly structures the book around instructions to set goals, remove business activities, build a scalable model and create a team. Its main purpose is applying a business-growth method. Accessible stories do not exempt it from hard exclusion 2. This is the 2025 Hardy–Erickson work, not Mark Roberge's different book with the same title.
